questions.q: Which word means the same as "purchase"?
Which is the polite way to interrupt a customer?
options: Sorry to interrupt, may I ask one quick question?
Hold on, I need to say something to you right now.
Wait a second, let me talk first, then you continue.
Excuse me, you are saying it wrong.

questions.q: A customer says, "I'll get back to you." What do they mean?
A customer says, "The parcel came, but the box was empty." What is the problem?
options: Nothing was inside the delivered package
It went to the wrong address

questions.q: Which line best confirms an email address on a call?
options: Okay, I have noted your email, thank you so much.
Your email is saved, we will send it soon.
Please type your email in the chat box later.
Let me read it back: r-a-v-i at gmail dot com. Is that right?

questions.q: Which sentence politely asks a customer to check their address?
options: You must give the address now.
Could you please confirm your delivery address?

questions.q: What does "pending" mean in "Your request is pending"?
A customer says, "To be honest, I'm not happy with the service." How do they feel?
You gave a customer wrong information earlier in the call. What do you say?
options: That was the system's fault, not mine.
You must have heard me wrong before.
Let's forget what I said earlier.
I'm sorry, I made a mistake earlier. The correct detail is this.

questions.q: You must transfer a call to billing. What do you say first?
options: Please call the billing number yourself.
I'll connect you to our billing team. Please stay on the line.
Wait, I'm sending you somewhere else.

questions.q: Choose: "Neither the manager nor the agents ___ aware of the change."
Choose the correct reported speech for: He said, "I am busy."
options: He said that he was busy.
He said that I am busy.
He said that he is being busy.

questions.q: Which word fits: "We will ___ your refund within five working days."
In a flat voice, a customer says, "Fine, whatever, just do it." What is the best way to read this?
options: They are likely annoyed; check they agree with the plan
They are fully happy with the plan
They want to cancel the order
They are asking for a manager

questions.q: Which is the most tactful way to tell a customer their due date is wrong?
options: I can see why that's confusing. The bill shows the 10th.
No, that is wrong. Please read your bill again carefully.
Everyone knows the due date is the 10th.
You have made a mistake about the date.

questions.q: The issue isn't solved yet and you must end the call. Which closing is best?
options: Okay, that's all from my side, have a nice day.
So, ticket 4471 is raised and I'll call you by 5 pm tomorrow.
We'll see what happens, someone may call you.
Please call again tomorrow and ask for an update.

task.title: Explain a delivery delay to a customer
task.brief: Speak your answer out loud for 60–90 seconds, as if you are on the call. Situation: Mr. Arjun Nair calls about a mixer grinder he ordered. It was due today, but it is delayed by three days because of heavy rain. The new delivery date is Friday. You can send him a tracking link by SMS. A good answer: greets him politely, says sorry for the delay, explains the reason and the new date in simple English, offers the SMS tracking link, asks if he has any other question, and closes politely. Use full, correct sentences and speak at a steady pace.
key_points: Asks if anything else is needed and closes politely

rubric.label: Greeting and structure
rubric.guide: 0 = no greeting or order, 3 = greets but misses steps, 5 = greets, explains, offers help and closes in order

rubric.label: Grammar and words
rubric.guide: 0 = many errors that confuse the meaning, 3 = some errors but clear, 5 = correct sentences and the right words

rubric.label: Politeness
rubric.guide: 0 = rude or abrupt, 3 = polite but flat, 5 = warm, respectful and uses please, sorry and thank you naturally

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = mostly clear, 5 = the reason, new date and next step are easy to understand
